name: The City of Aeyefall
description: Aeyefall, once Outumn’s capital, still shows traces of its oppressive past. Now, the city blends grand stone structures with newer, elegant wooden buildings, their bright roofs symbolizing the people’s spirit. Though its past splendor has faded, Aeyefall thrives with its timber and woodcraft, thanks to the nearby Shortfall Forest. Atop the city’s tallest cliff sits an eerie citadel. Formerly the home of Outumn’s Imperial Governor, it’s now a haunting reminder of dark times. Years ago, Imperial Wizards experimented on prisoners within its depths, in search to advance the methods of creating brainwashed Ironhand soldiers. These cruel trials left tormented spirits, who now roam its halls. These spirits are able to take control of dead bodies and rise as undead, making the citadel’s dungeons dangerous. While there have been attempts to exorcize them, the spirits keep returning. Protective sigils, supervised by the Celestianist Church, now seal the citadel. Yet, the Republic wizards are arguing that these ghosts may hold the last remains of knowledge about the Imperial Wizards research, which could potentially free thousands of Ironhand soldiers from the Empire’s mind control. This sparks tension between the wizards wanting research and the Church and the city watch who want to keep the citadel sealed. The Church seeks ways to purify the citadel, but what binds the spirits remains a mystery. Some think an artifact hidden in the citadel might be the cause; others feel the souls’ desire vengeance. A lasting solution eludes the clerics. Secretly, a powerful vampire, Lord Krox (NE vampire, with access to all spells of an archmage), resides in the Citadel. A formidable archmage in life, he is able to bypass the Church’s barriers, and has made the citadel his fortress. The old governor’s home is now his opulent den where he brings his victims. His intentions remain unclear, but he seems to feed only on individuals whom he sees as a disruption to Aeyefall, while his goal involves restoring the city to its former prestige for unclear reasons.
